Landing page + Supabase auth + rotation script (WARD 08)

- Landing: full copilot vision with hero/roadmap/trust sections, lp- prefixed ids, mode-boot/landing/app body-class state machine
- Auth: Supabase email+password (flowType implicit), guest button, sign-out keeps ward-history, vendored supabase-js 2.112.1
- api.py: GET /vendor/supabase.js route
- rotateByAttestation.ts: fetches /attestation, pre-flights iat/exp, submits via non-owner signers[1]
- hardhat.config.ts: optional NONOWNER_KEY in coston2 accounts
- Tests: 37/37 agent, 24/24 contracts

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

UI: Flare Ember redesign with live FTSO ticker

Three-pane crypto-terminal look (rail / chat / envelope review) with a
live green/red FTSO price ticker (FLR, BTC, ETH, XRP, USDC via new GET
/feeds — the same oracle Guardian enforces against). On narrow screens
the review pane becomes a slide-in drawer with pinned close, backdrop
and reopen pill. Meta questions ("what can you do?") get a local about
card instead of a policy refusal; refusal cards hint at what Ward can
sign.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

UI: chat + tx-review card served by the attested agent itself

Single static page at GET /: natural-language chat, attestation badge
decoding the live Google-signed token, signed-envelope cards with every
guarantee, policy-refusal and out-of-mandate cards, wallet connect
(MetaMask + Coston2 auto-add), Execute button (approval check +
guardian.execute via POST /execute-calldata), and localStorage history
that survives refresh. Verified end-to-end on Coston2: envelope from
live intent executed through the new Guardian (block 33558558).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

Deploy attestation stack to Coston2; agent image v3

Guardian redeployed at 0x5FCDc267ca392B64362957b7FD021719466d1775 (the
old deployment predates rotateSignerByAttestation). WardAttestor at
0xD06059f36cB6fc2737977f1445c95713f6a85b0F with all four live Google
JWKS keys registered, required config pinned to agent image v3
(sha256:a1626f08...), wired via setAttestor. Both explorer-verified.
Agent config, tests, and TEE VM metadata now point at the new stack.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

Attestation on-chain: trustless ward signer rotation via Google-signed TEE tokens

WardAttestor (vendored/trimmed from flare-vtpm-attestation, MIT) verifies
Confidential Space tokens on-chain: RS256 vs registered Google JWKS keys,
claims vs required config (TDX, secboot, exact image digest), exp/iat.
Key change vs reference: attestation binds to the eat_nonce claim (the
enclave signer address, inside the signed payload) instead of msg.sender,
so anyone may relay a token and replays are harmless.

Guardian.rotateSignerByAttestation lets anyone rotate wardSigner to the
attested enclave key. Tests verify the real captured token (24 passing).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

Capture Google Confidential Space JWKS snapshot as test fixture

The key matching attestation_sample.json's kid is still in rotation;
snapshotting it lets attestation tests verify the real Google-signed
token without a live VM.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

Intent layer: Gemini parses natural language, policy engine still decides

POST /intent turns free text into a structured draft via Gemini (structured
output, temperature 0) — parsing only; token/amount validation, planning,
policy checks, and signing stay deterministic. In the TEE, Vertex AI is
authenticated by the enclave's service account so no API key enters the
attested image. Live-tested: swap signed, transfer refused as unsupported,
over-cap swap refused by policy with parsed intent echoed back.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

TEE: agent live in Confidential Space (Intel TDX), enclave key enforced on-chain

Dockerized agent runs in a production Confidential Space VM; ephemeral
wardSigner generated inside the enclave, bound into Google's attestation
token as eat_nonce, and rotated into Guardian on Coston2. E2E re-run with
the envelope signed remotely by the TEE: executed on-chain, tamper refused.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

E2E on Coston2: signed envelope executed through Guardian, tamper refused

deployMocks.ts deploys mock USDC/WFLR + MockDEX with rate derived from live
FTSO prices. E2E script: agent quotes and signs, user executes through
Guardian (100 USDC -> 15781 WFLR, minOut honored, block 33428585); the same
envelope with drainApproval calldata reverts SelectorNotAllowed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

Agent: policy engine + EIP-712 envelope signer with on-chain hash parity

Python agent (uv, FastAPI): structured swap intent -> FTSO-quoted plan ->
deterministic policy check (spend caps, target/selector allowlist, slippage,
deadline) -> signed Safety Envelope. Quote math mirrors Guardian's oracle
floor exactly; parity test asserts the local EIP-712 digest equals the
deployed Guardian.hashEnvelope() on Coston2. 19 tests.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

README: add Coston2 deployment details (verified Guardian address)

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

Guardian: enforce FTSO fair-value floor at execution time

minOut is the agent's promise at signing time; this adds the chain's
own check at execution time. Envelopes now carry feedIn/feedOut FTSO
feed IDs and maxSlippageBps: Guardian reads both USD prices from
FTSO v2 when the swap lands and reverts if the fill is worse than
fair value minus the allowed slippage — catching fills that clear a
stale or lenient minOut. Handles differing feed and token decimals.

Adds MockFtsoV2, five oracle test cases (13 passing total), and a
Coston2 deploy script that resolves FtsoV2 via the ContractRegistry.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

Ward: Guardian contract enforcing TEE-signed Safety Envelopes

Guardian executes transactions only within the guarantees of an
EIP-712 SafetyEnvelope signed by the Ward agent: spend cap, target +
selector allowlist, minOut, deadline, single-use nonce. Includes
MockDEX test harness and an 8-case test suite (all passing) covering
sandwich protection, replay, tampering, and caller checks.

Contracts workspace is based on flare-foundation/flare-hardhat-starter
(Coston2 target). Tenderly auto-wrapping disabled via env flag so
ethers contract objects keep their ABI methods in tests.

Built for the Flare Summer Signal hackathon, Confidential Compute track.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
